items.content_excerpt: Ondas shares could experience an approximately 11% move following the company’s November 12 earnings report, scheduled before the market opens, according to Bloomberg options data. The stock has moved more than options implied in four of its last eight earnings releases, indicating substantial volatility around quarterly results. Historical data highlight several significant surprises: on May 14, options implied a 9.6% move, but the stock fluctuated 20%; on August 12, 2025, an expected 7.5% move was followed by a massive 60.7% swing. On May 15, 2025, shares moved 13.7% versus an implied 7.1%, while the March 12, 2025 report triggered a 20% decline despite options pricing in just a 2.1% move. By contrast, some earnings releases produced smaller-than-expected reactions, including a 0.5% move versus 9.3% implied in August. These historical discrepancies suggest options markets may underestimate the stock’s potential volatility ahead of the upcoming results. $ONDS

items.title: U.S. stock futures edged higher Thursday night, signaling a potential rebound after growing concerns over tighter AI regulation and data-cen
items.content_excerpt: U.S. stock futures edged higher Thursday night, signaling a potential rebound after growing concerns over tighter AI regulation and data-center construction triggered Wall Street’s worst session in nearly 19 months. S&P 500 futures rose 0.26% to 7,402, while Nasdaq 100 futures gained 0.83% to 26,970.50. Dow futures slipped 0.15% to 51,537. Thursday’s sell-off was led by semiconductor stocks, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunging 12.25%. Nvidia fell nearly 10% and AMD dropped 17%, while Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet lost 2%–4%. Apple declined a more modest 1.5%. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 5.5%, the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Dow lost 3.4%. Investor concerns intensified after Democrats secured majorities in both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations of stricter AI regulation. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa called for a pause on new data-center construction until stronger consumer protections are established. $NVDA $AMD $MSFT

items.content_excerpt: $SPY $NVDA May be taking a chunk of $POET soon when the dust settles 43 of 47 data center moratoriums on ballots across the country passed Market is pricing in data centers not being built However, data centers will be built - but they will be built Asia instead Indirectly bullish for POET since, in Singapore, they will be in the heart of the future global Silicon Valley of AI infrastructure Pretty sad though that all the billions of US dollars in future investment will be instead be allocated to Asia though There is a $META data center about five miles from my house and they are always hiring for a huge list of six figure positions Meta also recently initiated the America’s Workforce Academy (AWA) which is a program designed to train workers for skilled-trade and infrastructure roles building its AI data centers The program is about a month long, and is 100% free for participants; Meta covers all tuition, travel (airfare), lodging, and provides a daily stipend or paycheck during the program - also no experience is needed Have my electricity costs skyrocketed due to the Meta data center by my house? No Would I even know it’s there and not just another warehouse if I wasn’t told it’s a data center? Honestly, no Are there brand new neighborhoods, restaurants, and entertainment districts popping up everywhere around me due to the data center and influx of jobs? Yes Increased supply of housing puts pressure on rising home costs, btw The anti-data center movement is propaganda IMO As I said in an earlier post, data centers have been being built everywhere for almost 20 years and nobody cared - the recent hate is caused by preying on ignorance and anxiety via TikToks Loop in the term “billionaires” and it’s easy to sway emotions… Anyways, all the great those opportunities the next industrial revolution is providing are probably going to be shipped to China now There is a reason why $BABA closed up 3% and $SPY closed down 4% I’m not even angry, just bummed out to be honest

items.content_excerpt: $SOFI From 10-Q, * The 2026 converts were paid entirely in cash. On October 15, SoFi settled the remaining $428.0 million principal balance with cash. No common shares were issued, and the related capped calls expired worthless. * This resolves the previously outstanding settlement question. The notes had represented up to 19.1 million potential shares, approximately 1.47% of the 1.297 billion shares outstanding at quarter-end. * SoFiUSD faces a new regulatory transition requirement. Starting January 18, 2027, existing issuance by SoFi Bank is not grandfathered. Issuance must move to a bank subsidiary separately approved as a permitted payment-stablecoin issuer. * SoFi says the OCC has not yet announced when it will accept these applications. SoFi intends to apply and seek a temporary waiver, but warns that failure to obtain timely approval or a waiver could require it to suspend or stop issuing SoFiUSD. SoFiUSD remains financially small today: $73.5 million outstanding

items.content_excerpt: $SLS Angelos M. Stergiou CEO - 10,000 I think if I can just chime in for one second, Li, to add on to what Dr. Jamy just said -- in our research that have done in the U.S.. EUS and Japan only, once you funnel through the treatment landscape, that allows for about 10,000 patients or so that would be eligible in the CR2 maintenance phase. Even venetoclax and hypomethylate-you heard from Dr. Jamy, but also previously from Dr. Levy, it's still in that 6, 7, 8 months' time frame. So more and more drugs have gotten patients into remission. Unfortunately, those ineligible or unable to get transplanted just don't do well, and that's where we hope GPS will make a significant impact.

items.content_excerpt: DraftKings reported disappointing Q3 2026 results, with an adjusted loss of $0.53 per share versus the $0.36 loss expected by analysts, while revenue reached $1.33B, missing the $1.41B consensus despite growing 16% year over year. Adjusted EBITDA deteriorated significantly to -$316.9M, compared with -$126.5M a year earlier, reflecting sharply higher investment spending, particularly in its Predictions business. The company also cut its FY2026 revenue guidance to $6.35B–$6.55B, implying a $6.45B midpoint below analysts’ $6.65B expectations. Its 2027 adjusted EBITDA outlook of $800M–$1B also fell well short of the roughly $1.12B anticipated by Wall Street. DraftKings expects its Predictions segment to generate adjusted EBITDA losses of $650M–$700M for full-year 2026, highlighting the substantial near-term costs of expanding this business. $DKNG

Ondas shares could experience an approximately 11% move following the company’s November 12 earnings report, scheduled before the market opens, according to Bloomberg options data. The stock has moved more than options implied in four of its last eight earnings releases, indicating substantial volatility around quarterly results. Historical data highlight several significant surprises: on May 14, options implied a 9.6% move, but the stock fluctuated 20%; on August 12, 2025, an expected 7.5% move was followed by a massive 60.7% swing. On May 15, 2025, shares moved 13.7% versus an implied 7.1%, while the March 12, 2025 report triggered a 20% decline despite options pricing in just a 2.1% move. By contrast, some earnings releases produced smaller-than-expected reactions, including a 0.5% move versus 9.3% implied in August. These historical discrepancies suggest options markets may underestimate the stock’s potential volatility ahead of the upcoming results. $ONDS
